newsitem.title: ITALY: Treu denies plan to bring Italy '98 budget forward.
newsitem.headline: Treu denies plan to bring Italy '98 budget forward.

text.p: Italy's Minister of Labour Tiziano Treu on Thursday denied that some measures from Italy's 1998 financial budget could be brought forward into this year to help the nation meet the criteria to join Europe's single currency.

"We must put forward a structural budget and it will be in 1998, we are not talking about 1997 but 1998, and the budget will come into force at the start of next year," Treu said while attending a conference here.

On Wednesday, Italy's regional affairs minister Franco Bassannini said parts of Italy's 1998 financial budget could be brought forward to ensure Italy meets the parameters for entry to Europe's Economic Monetary Union (EMU).

Treu would not comment on the size of the 1998 budget saying that the government had until the end of May to decide. On Wednesday, Italy's budget undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta said the government plans up to a 20 trillion lire 1998 budget.

The European Commission estimated Italy's deficit to GDP ratio at 3.2 percent for 1997 on Wednesday compared to a three percent EMU target. Treu said the result could vary between 2.8 percent and 3.4 percent, but he thought it would be towards 2.8 percent.
